Identify the presence of radiative or kinetic extinction."},{"function":"combustion fundamentals","statement":"The work measures flame temperature, size, and color and tests whether steady spherical diffusion flames exist and extinguish near 1130 K.","quote":"Microgravity spherical diffusion flames extinguish when the peak temperature first decreases below 1130 K."}],"statements":[{"statement":"The fuels are ethylene (C2H4) and methane (CH4).","quote":"Obtain detailed measurements in quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames for C2H4 and CH4."},{"statement":"The geometries include normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames and normal and inverse coflow flames.","quote":"Obtain similar limits and temperatures for inverse and normal coflow flames."},{"statement":"The varied parameters are flow rate, stoichiometric mixture fraction, amount of N2 or CO2, and pressure.","quote":"as functions of flow rate, Zst, amount of inert (N2 or CO2), and pressure for C2H4 and CH4 flames."},{"statement":"A stated hypothesis is extinction once the peak temperature first decreases below 1130 K.","quote":"Microgravity spherical diffusion flames extinguish when the peak temperature first decreases below 1130 K."},{"statement":"Soot formation is hypothesized to need a local C/O ratio and temperature above critical values and a sufficiently low strain rate.","quote":"Soot formation requires a region where local C/O ratio and T exceed their critical values, and where strain rate is sufficiently low."}]}
